parsed.why: National document and entry restrictions apply directly; a nationally imposed facilities ban and arrests add exposure, despite no locally enacted ban. The local low-risk label is fragile under national override.

The shared national restrictions are compounded by an enforced state facilities ban, complaint reporting and a visitor-unfriendly documentary defence. Protections and lack of private-venue coverage limit, but do not remove, exposure.

National document and entry risks remain, but local nondiscrimination and hate-crime protections operate alongside no mapped facilities ban. These are meaningful local mitigations, not protection from national rules.

Robust local nondiscrimination and care protections mitigate the national travel-facing restrictions, but documented shortfalls for incarcerated trans people and unresolved facilities access leave material uncertainty.

National entry and document restrictions remain, but enforceable shield laws protect visiting care-seekers, public-accommodation protections apply to visitors, and facilities rules include gender-neutral single-user bathrooms.
